title: Backspace String Compare
statement: Two coworkers each type a note into a buggy text box. The strings s and t record their exact keystrokes: each lowercase letter is a typed character, and each '#' is a backspace that deletes the character typed immediately before it. Pressing backspace when the text is already empty does nothing. Simulate the typing of each string to obtain its final rendered text, then return True if the two rendered texts are identical and False otherwise. For example, s = 'ab#c' renders to 'ac' and t = 'ad#c' also renders to 'ac', so the answer is True.
hints: Instead of reasoning about backspaces globally, what if you replayed the keystrokes one at a time, keeping only the text that survives?
A stack models the rendered text perfectly: push each letter, and on '#' pop the top only if the stack is non-empty (a backspace on empty text is a no-op).
Write a helper that renders a keystroke string to its final text via the stack, run it on both s and t, and return whether the two results are equal.
